Subject: Follow-up & ask: SDK quickstart, routing, embeddings/re-ranker

Rachel — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can scope POC: 

- Use case: customer support triage + auto-respond drafts; want a reranker over candidate replies and embeddings for ticket clustering.
- Expected traffic: ~12 qps avg with bursts to 30 qps.
- Latency target: 200ms p50 for first-token on fast paths; willing to sacrifice some p99 for cost.

Immediate asks: 
1) A short SDK quickstart (Python + TypeScript) we can run locally to exercise auth, routing between models (low-cost vs low-latency), and structured output/tool-calling examples.
2) Guidance on auth options: short-lived keys for POC, how to rotate, or whether we should use mTLS for Dedicated.
3) Recommended embedding + reranker setup for short ticket bodies (~100 tokens) and how to test quality locally.

If you can send a sample app and a short list of next steps (including any required access/trial creds), we can plan an internal engineering spike next week.

Thanks,
Amit

Subject: Re: Follow-up & ask: SDK quickstart, routing, embeddings/re-ranker

Thanks — adding details for the POC tech plan and local test notes. Long but meant to be actionable.

Auth & local testing- - - - -
1) For POC: short-lived API keys are easiest. We issue a token with "exp" of 72 hours. Rotation pattern: client requests a new ephemeral key from a small bootstrap endpoint we provide (requires verifying a stable admin email), or you can generate keys in the console. For production Dedicated or Private, we recommend mTLS or OAuth with a short-lived client certificate.

2) Local dev: the quickstart will include a lightweight env file (.env.example) and a helper script (redwood auth:fetch-token) that stores tokens in a local credential store. The TS sample will show using native fetch with the Authorization: Bearer header; Python will use requests.Session with automatic retry/backoff.

Routing and model selection- - - - -
1) Best practice: tag models with performance and cost profiles (e.g., rdx-fast-v1, rdx-cost-v2). The SDK supports a route selector: routeBy({ latencySLO: 200, costPreference: 'balanced' }). If a fast model is unavailable, runtime falls back to the next compatible variant.

2) Implementation note: for your ticket triage flow, send short context + 1-2 shots. Use continuous batching for throughput and set max_tokens low for faster first token. We’ll include sample route configs in the repo.

Embeddings & reranker- - - - -
1) For short tickets (~100 tokens) we recommend 1024-d float16 embeddings from the rdx-embed-compact family. Indexing: approximate nearest neighbors (HNSW) for speed. We’ll include a small script that builds an index from local CSV and runs reranker candidates through a cheap generative filter then a cross-encoder rerank (we provide a hosted cross-encoder variant).

2) Testing quality locally: the sample will include a set of labeled ticket queries (100 rows) and an evaluation script that outputs MRR and recall@5. You can tweak embedding dimensionality or switch to a quantized variant for lower RAM.

Structured output & tool calling- - - - -
1) We’ll include a JSON schema example for the reply-draft generator: {"action":"string","priority":"enum","suggested_text":"string"} and a tool-call stub that simulates creating a support reply via POST /internal/tickets/:id/replies.

2) The TS sample app demonstrates streaming responses and progressive UI updates (first token), while the Python sample includes a CLI to run evals and reranker tests.

Attachments in repo: sample-ts-app.tar.gz, quickstart scripts, local index builder.

I’ll upload the sample repo to the GitHub link Rachel included and add run instructions.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
